name: The training workbench
summary: The place in the game where the player decides what the learning robot is rewarded for, and sees how its learning is going. Five plates on a bench she buys and sets down: the dials, what it sees, the nameplate, the charts, the likes-and-dislikes grid. Approved whole by the CEO on 2026-09-10 (Q-101) after he saw the mockups.
requirements: Every number on the bench is read from the robot's own state or computed in front of her — never a story about training
Reward values are per robot, and a dial turn goes through the gateway so a replay reproduces it
Negatives are allowed on every row; the bench draws the consequence rather than forbidding it
The bench's charts and the robot's own scorecard are one drawing language
Words on the nameplate only; numerals on axes; pictures everywhere else
Nothing expensive runs when a page opens
current_status: Built on main as of 2026-09-10 and deployed to the tablet: all five plates, the bench in the shop, the dial turn as a replayed verb with a CC0 click on it, the crate that remembers a robot's practice when she moves it, and the proof tests. Both suites, the gateway check and the robot session green on a clean checkout; the robot's learning numbers unchanged. Open for the CEO: Q-102, which of three dial sounds (one is wired now). Parked by him: whether the game wants a pixel face, until he has seen the plates in action. Left for the release: the release notes and the tag.
